extracted.intended_audience: NIH extramural research community — investigators, applicants, institutional research administrators, and other stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: A news/index page providing short updates, reminders, and resources about NIH grants policies, review processes, and application requirements for extramural researchers and administrators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select models appropriate to the research question (NAMs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators should still select the models most appropriate for their specific research questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH supports a wide range of scientifically sound approaches to advance understanding of human health and disease and encourages approaches that enhance human relevance and translational potential (e.g., New Approach Methodologies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow PF5 application format and understand linked award splitting
rubrics_metrics.description: Watch NIH’s 6-minute overview of the new Collaborative International Research Project (PF5) award structure to learn key features, application format, and how applications may be split into linked awards after review and before Just-in-Time requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should use the specified PF5 application format and be aware that, following review, applications may be split into linked awards prior to Just-in-Time, so plan project structure and budgets accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the 2026 Pilot Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plan format
rubrics_metrics.description: We have issued a new 2026 Pilot DMS Plan format based on a simplified set of required elements to use when preparing Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing DMS Plans, follow the 2026 pilot format and include the simplified required elements specified in that format (the announcement indicates a standardized/simplified set of required elements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasize replication and reproducibility in applications and awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Embedding replication and reproducibility throughout NIH research: key reminders for applications, awards, and a new highlighted topic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH’s Gold Standard Science plan encourages a culture that values replication and reproducibility; applicants should consider replication/reproducibility practices and related plans where relevant to strengthen proposals and align with NIH priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand review outcome category: 'Competitive But Not Discussed'
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that some strong applications may fall below a 33% cut off and the middle third of applications in a study section were designated as 'competitive but not discussed.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants receiving this designation should understand it reflects the review scoring/cutoff processes (e.g., centralized review modifications) and may indicate a competitive score despite not being discussed; consult NIH resources for implications and next steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be aware of centralized peer review implications
rubrics_metrics.description: Centralized NIH peer review has been implemented within the Center for Scientific Review (CSR) to strengthen efficiency, competition, and transparency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants and institutions should be aware that peer review consolidation may change study section processes, review timelines, and how applications are evaluated; monitor NIH notices and Nexus updates for specifics on how centralization affects review and outcomes.
